title: Synchron
summary: US/Australian developer of an endovascular brain-computer interface.
bodyHtml:
Investment Thesis

Synchron's Stentrode is delivered through the jugular vein and expanded inside a blood vessel next to the motor cortex, avoiding open-brain surgery. That design trades channel count for procedural safety, which matters for patients with paralysis who need a reliable cursor and switching interface rather than high-resolution control. The company has run early human trials in the US and Australia and is pursuing a pivotal pathway.

Technology Exposure

  • Stentrode endovascular implant
  • Cursor and device-control software
  • Clinical trial programme

What To Watch

  • Pivotal trial enrolment and outcomes
  • Durability of signal over years
  • Competition from higher-channel implants

Record Notes

Editorial brief compiled 19 November 2026 from company disclosures, agency publications and press reporting. Figures are as reported by those sources and have not been independently audited; no live market data is used.

businessMeaning: If a vein can deliver a usable signal, BCI becomes a catheter-lab procedure rather than neurosurgery, which changes the addressable patient pool.
investmentLens: Private; the strategic question is whether lower bandwidth is enough for communication and control use cases.
